description_short: Cross-table fluorocarbon query linking SiO2 ALE Tables I and II to retrieve near-RT etch conditions with ion-energy windows for shared fluorocarbon precursors.

paper.title: Atomic Layer Etching of SiO2 for Nanoscale Semiconductor Devices: A Review

tables_modeled.label: Table I
tables_modeled.description: Overview of SiO2 ALE chemistries including fluorocarbon-based fluorination steps.

tables_modeled.label: Table II
tables_modeled.description: SiO2 ALE process window summary including removal gases, process temperature, etch rate, and ion-energy window.

properties_used.label: Fluorocarbon precursor
properties_used.role: Linking key between Tables I and II; normalized to a base precursor token for joining.

properties_used.label: Removal gas
properties_used.role: Identifies the gas used in the removal step in Table II.

properties_used.label: Process temperature (°C)
properties_used.role: Removal-step process temperature, parsed to filter near-RT conditions (RT ± 20 °C).

properties_used.label: Etching rate
properties_used.role: Numerical etch rate used to sort conditions in descending order.

properties_used.label: Ion-energy window
properties_used.role: Specifies the ion-energy range for the removal step in Table II.

aggregation.grouping_key: shared fluorocarbon precursor base across Tables I and II
aggregation.description: Rows are produced for all conditions in Table II whose fluorocarbon precursor base token also appears in Table I.

output_shape.description: One row per joined fluorocarbon process condition near RT.
columns: precursor: normalized fluorocarbon precursor (label if available, otherwise base token).
removal: removal gas used in the ion-assisted or plasma step.
process_temp: textual representation of the process temperature from Table II.
etch_rate: numeric etching rate parsed from the Table II entry.
ion_energy_window: textual ion energy window describing the energy range of the removal step.

postprocessing_notes.interpretation: The result links fluorocarbon-based fluorination chemistries (Table I) with detailed process conditions and ion-energy windows (Table II) under near-RT conditions, enabling comparison of how different fluorocarbon plasmas perform in SiO2 ALE around room temperature.
